forms.title: Basic Mechanical Trouble Shooting

forms.footer_title: Basic Mechanical Trouble Shooting — Blaster/Vacuum Truck Skills Assessment
forms.instructions: Please rate the Overall skill using 1-5 (1 Low and 5 High). Under the Needs column, please indicate any sub skill that needs further development (a, b, c, …). Then provide any comments you feel necessary.

sections.title: Pump Overview
items: Know the difference between your RPM's and PSI

items.text: Not Enough Pressure at the End of the Hose
subitems: Make sure all hoses are tight
Check to see if nozzle is tight and not clogged
Shut down pump and tighten belts. Do not operate if they are making a squealing sound.
Check to ensure water is not running onto belts causing them to slip
Change it but make sure you have the correct rupture disk for the correct type of pump and brand
Damaged hoses on Pump (should be replaced as soon as possible)
Note: if your hose starts bouncing around, the water could be low
Hose may have become detached from the filter pot or just placed inside the tank
Adjust water level so the level stays where it should be (not exiting the tank)
Check water level – if low, check filter bag
If tank is full of water, check packing. Open plunger box if water is spraying out the packing is blown
If none of the above, drop head and check for debris in valve

items.text: Pump Engine suddenly begins to die
subitems: If you have fuel filter, you may need to change it
Check Bag House – Most likely need to be changed
If outside temperature is above 90°F this could be the cause. Get a water hose and barely open the valve. Position water flow onto the radiator.
Truck could have an alternator problem and the batteries are about to fail

forms.notes: Title is printed on two lines ('Technician II → Technician III' / 'Skill Assessment') and is joined here. Header fields (Employee/Office/Trainer/Evaluation Date) are printed ABOVE the title. An extra intro line precedes the instructions: 'The topics included are: LOTO, PPE, Vacuuming, Confined Space, Hydroblasting, and Safety.' Items use bullets (•) with hollow-bullet (o) sub-items and one third level (▪) instead of letters, even though the instruction refers to (a, b, c, …). Each topic is its own table row with its own Rating/Needs/Comments cells. No section heading paragraphs; the section title is the second column header. Sign-off has only Trainer, Employee, Date. Under 'Basic Set Up of Vac Job', the line 'understanding the uses of different types of vacuum hose' has no bullet but sits at sub-bullet indent; kept as its own sub-item. Kept verbatim: 'Flangless' (likely 'Flangeless'); 'O' bullet markers normalized to 'o'.

conventions.items: Each item is a string, or {text, subitems} when the source nests sub-items under it. Leading letters/bullets ('a.', 'i.', '1.', '•', 'o', '▪') are removed; order is preserved, so letters can be re-derived from position (restarting at a. within each level).
conventions.kind: 'rated' = one overall 1-5 rating for the section plus a Needs flag per sub-item and comments. 'rated-per-item' = the Rating column lists a blank per sub-item letter (a.____ b.____ ...), i.e. each sub-item is rated individually.
conventions.layout: 'row-per-item' = one table row (own Needs/Comments cells) per sub-item; 'single-cell' = all sub-items in one cell with one Needs/Comments cell for the section (Needs is written as item letters); 'row-per-topic' = one table row (own Rating/Needs/Comments cells) per top-level topic, sub-items listed in that row.
conventions.part: Heading paragraph printed above a group of sections (e.g. 'Vacuum Truck'), when it differs from the section title.
